LEANING LAMP POST IN THE COBBLED LANE: an old iron lamp post leaning slightly at the bend of a narrow cobbled lane, crooked timber-framed houses tilting toward each other above it, a round lit window under the nearest gable, the lane curving away between overhanging eaves, a chimney with a bend in it rising above the roofline

LIT ROUND WINDOW ON THE CURVED LANE: a round glowing window set into the plaster front of a crooked cottage at the bend of a cobbled lane, timber-framed houses leaning close on either side, the lane winding away between them into a cluster of pointed gables, a tiny balcony with flower boxes above the window

IVY ARCH AT THE LANE'S END: a stone arch with ivy trailing over its keystone spanning a narrow cobbled lane, old plaster and timber-framed houses pressing close on both sides, the lane receding through the arch between stepped gables, a corner lantern with a coloured glass shade hanging just inside the passage

CORNER LANTERN ON THE COBBLED BEND: a corner lantern with a green glass shade mounted on a bracket at the turn of a narrow cobbled lane, crooked timber-framed houses leaning over the stone below, a round lit window under a pointed roof opposite, the lane curling away between old plaster fronts into deeper gables

ARCHWAY UNDER THE FISH WEATHERVANE: a low stone arch with a weathervane shaped like a fish on the gable above it, at the entrance to a cobbled lane, crooked half-timbered houses crowding either side, a lit round window gleaming under the nearest gable, the lane bending away behind the arch between leaning walls, a striped awning furled above a green door

HUMPED BRIDGE ON THE CANAL STREET: a small humped stone bridge with a lantern on each parapet crossing a narrow canal, tall thin houses with stepped gables standing along the water, two moored punts resting beneath the arch, a lit doorway with a striped awning visible at the far end of the canalside flagstones

LANTERN-LIT DOORWAY ON THE CANAL: a deep stone doorway hung with a lantern of amber glass at the edge of a canal street, tall narrow houses with crow-stepped gables receding along the water, a small humped bridge visible further along the flagstones, a moored punt resting against the stone embankment below the doorway

LIT WINDOW DOUBLED ON THE CANAL: a tall narrow lit window in a thin canal-side house reflected whole in the water below, a row of stepped-gable houses receding along the flagstone embankment, a small humped bridge with a single lantern crossing the canal further along, a moored punt tied at the foot of worn stone steps

SMALL HUMPED BRIDGE OVER THE CANAL: a mossy stone humped bridge with a lamp post on each parapet arching over a still canal, tall narrow houses with pointed and crow-stepped gables lining both banks, flagstones running along the water, a lantern-lit doorway with a wooden boot hung on an iron bracket above it on the far bank

LAMP AT THE TOP OF THE HILLSIDE STAIR: a single old iron lamp post standing at the highest landing of a broad stone stair climbing between close-packed houses, worn stone steps descending in a curve below it, shuttered plaster cottages pressing in on both sides, a round lit window glowing in the gable of the house at the summit

STONE STAIR CLIMBING BETWEEN HOUSES: a long worn stone stair rising steeply between plaster and brick houses with pointed roofs and crooked chimneys, a lamp post at each landing, the stair turning at a corner turret with a hat-shaped roof, flower boxes on a tiny balcony overhanging the middle steps

LAMP POST AT THE STAIR'S LANDING: an iron lamp post standing at a mid-stair landing on a hillside stone stair, worn steps climbing away above and below it between timber-framed houses with leaning gables, a round lit window under the nearest pointed roof, a spiral stone stair visible through an open arch in the wall beside the landing

LANTERN-HUNG ARCADE ON THE OLD STREET: a vaulted stone arcade with a lantern hung under every arch stretching along a cobbled street, the street and its crooked plaster houses visible through the open arches, a corner turret with a hat-shaped roof rising beyond the far end of the arcade, a carved wooden fish hanging on a short chain beneath one of the inner arches

VAULTED ARCADE WITH COLOURED LANTERNS: a long vaulted stone arcade hung with lanterns of coloured glass under each arch, flagstones running beneath the vault, old plaster and brick buildings visible through the arches along the street beyond, a small round window set above the central arch of the passage

COVERED ARCADE OVER THE COBBLED LANE: a wide stone arcade with rounded vaults and a lantern at every pier covering a cobbled lane, the lane visible stretching away through the open side arches between old timber-framed houses, a striped awning hanging beneath one arch over a blue door, a round lit window gleaming at the arcade's far end

CREAM TRAM AT THE IRON SHELTER: a plain cream tram with a single round headlamp waiting at a small tram stop beneath a small plain wooden shelter with a curved tiled roof, cobblestones spread around it, old stone and plaster houses with crooked gables receding down the street behind, a lamp post leaning slightly at the near corner, a striped awning above a doorway to one side

TRAM WAITING BY THE LEANING LAMP: a plain cream tram with one round headlamp standing at a small plain wooden shelter with a curved tiled roof on a cobbled street, a leaning lamp post beside the shelter, old timber-framed and plaster houses with pointed gables receding behind the tram, a small rounded old car resting against the far kerb further down the street

TRAM STOP UNDER THE STEPPED GABLES: a plain cream tram with a single round headlamp at rest beneath a small plain wooden shelter with a curved tiled roof on a flagstone street, tall stone houses with crow-stepped gables standing close behind it, a lamp post at the near corner, a bicycle leaning against the wall of a plaster house beside the shelter

BAKEHOUSE ROUND WINDOW ON THE CORNER: a corner bakehouse with a big round lit window full of loaves set into its plaster front, a big wooden pretzel hanging on a bracket over its arched door, the cobbled street forking either side between old stone and timber-framed houses with crooked shutters, a lamp post leaning at the nearer fork

WOODEN PRETZEL OVER THE BAKEHOUSE DOOR: a big wooden pretzel hanging on a bracket above the arched door of a corner bakehouse, its round lit window glowing with loaves on the sill, cobblestones running away on both sides between old plaster houses with pointed and crooked gables, a tiny balcony with flower boxes overhanging the wall above the pretzel

BAKEHOUSE WINDOW ON THE COBBLED FORK: a corner bakehouse with a round lit window bright with loaves at a fork in a cobbled lane, a big wooden pretzel hanging on a bracket above its painted door, old timber-framed houses with leaning gables receding down each fork, a corner turret with a hat-shaped roof rising above the bakehouse itself

ARCHED BRIDGE OVER THE RIVER: an old stone arched bridge with a lamp post at each end spanning a wide river, old plaster and brick houses with stepped gables and pointed roofs standing close along the far bank, flagstones across the bridge deck, a lantern-lit doorway with an iron key hung on a bracket above it just beyond the far parapet

STONE BRIDGE WITH LAMPS ON EACH PARAPET: a broad old stone arch bridge with an iron lamp post on each parapet crossing a slow river, tall narrow houses with crow-stepped and pointed gables lining the far bank, worn stone steps descending to the water at one end, a striped awning hanging over a doorway in the nearest house beyond the bridge

STATION CANOPY OVER THE FLAGSTONE FORECOURT: a small old station with a broad canopy hung with lanterns at each post standing over a wide flagstone forecourt, a round lit window set into the station's pointed gable above the canopy, old plaster and brick houses with crooked rooflines receding on either side, a bicycle leaning against the station wall beneath the canopy's edge

LANTERN-LIT STATION CANOPY: a low station canopy with a lantern hung at every iron post sheltering a broad flagstone forecourt, a round window glowing in the gable of the station above, old stone houses with pointed roofs and crooked chimneys standing along the street leading away from the forecourt, a lamp post leaning at the forecourt's near corner
